answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: The operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes. This applies once the operator knows or should know that an accident involving a death has occurred. The call goes to the toll-free number 1-800-746-1553.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA immediately and within 15 minutes once the operator knows or should know of an accident involving a death.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the listed accidents.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. It is raised by 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane, but that increase applies only where methane is present.

claims.text: The combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must have an incombustible content of not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: The required percentage increases by 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane only where methane is present in a ventilating current.
claims.quote: Where methane is present in any ventilating current, the percent of incombustible content of such combined dust shall be increased 0.4 percent for each 0.1 percent of methane.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: The operator must make available to each miner going underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months. Each drill must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change, and it must involve all persons underground.

claims.text: Underground mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held to assess the ability of all persons underground to reach the surface or other designated points of safety within the time limits of the self-rescue devices that would be used during an actual emergency.

claims.text: Drills must be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties. About 8 of those hours are given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: Approximately 8 hours of the training are given at the minesite.
claims.quote: approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway. This applies in both surface (56.9300) and underground (57.9300) metal and nonmetal mine standards.

claims.text: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway (30 CFR 56.9300).
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: The same mid-axle height requirement appears in 30 CFR 57.9300.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air in a refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.

claims.text: Within the refuge alternative, the breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth OSHA requires a construction trench to have a protective system. They cover mine shaft and bucket requirements, not trench excavation rules.

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site. They cover MSHA training and certification rules, and they don't mention FAA requirements or drones.

answers.question: When does a mine need an EPA stormwater discharge permit for runoff from its site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say when a mine needs an EPA stormwater discharge permit. They cover impoundment design (30 CFR 77.216-2) and permits for mining under water (30 CFR 75.1716). Neither addresses EPA stormwater permits.
